conventions.convention: Unmarked logarithms are natural and information is in nats. For b>1, log_b(t)=ln(t)/ln(b); bits use b=2.
Zero entropy terms contribute zero. Finite KL is directional and equals +∞ when the first law has positive mass at a zero of the second law.
Conditional probability vectors are formed only at positive-mass conditioning values; conditional entropy omits zero-mass conditioning values.
Conditional mutual information averages conditional KL over positive-mass conditioning values. Conditional independence is required at every such value, with no condition imposed at zero-mass values.
The finite-to-measurable KL bridge explicitly assumes AC only for the published general KL interface; its finite density construction uses no choice.
Sharp Fano uses a same-alphabet estimate generated from Y and m≥2. The singleton case is separate; arbitrary finite output alphabets use the weaker erasure corollary.

load_bearing.statement: For finite nonnegative vectors a,b with sums A,B, the support-aware sum of a_i ln(a_i/b_i) is at least A ln(A/B). When A,B>0, equality holds exactly when a_i=(A/B)b_i for every i.
For finite probability vectors p,q on the same alphabet, D(p||q)≥0, and D(p||q)=0 if and only if p=q. If p_i>0=q_i for some coordinate, then D(p||q)=+∞.
Marginals of a joint pmf on finite nonempty alphabets are probability vectors. Conditionals at positive-mass values are probability vectors, as are their marginals.
For finite X,Y,Z, I(X;Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|Z)-H(X,Y|Z)≥0. Equality holds if and only if the conditional joint pmf factors at every positive-mass value of Z.
For finite X,Y,Z with a joint pmf, H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z) and I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z). In particular, I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X). All terms are finite.
For finite X→Y→Z under the stated positive-mass conditional factorization, I(X;Z)≤I(X;Y), with equality if and only if I(X;Y|Z)=0.
Assuming AC only for the published general KL interface, measurable-space KL for finite full-power-set laws equals the finite KL sum, with value +∞ exactly upon support failure.

alerts.finding: The Definition introduces the joint law P_{XYZ}, defines R by “R(C×A×B)=∫_C K(z,A)L(z,B) P_Z(dz)”, and then writes “I(X;Y|Z):=D(P_{XYZ}||R)”. The rectangle formula constructs R in coordinate order Z,X,Y, whereas P_{XYZ} is in order X,Y,Z. Its cited supplier lem-same-marginal-conditional-product-law-well-defined constructs the same Z-first law and supplies no permutation identification. KL requires two laws on the same measurable space. For distinct singleton value spaces X={0}, Y={1}, Z={2}, the displayed laws have different underlying product carriers. An explicit coordinate permutation or a consistently ordered reference law is missing.

Proof step 1.1 says “taking C equal to the whole Z space shows its Z marginal is P_Z.” In the displayed formula R(C×A×B)=∫_C K(z,A)L(z,B) P_Z(dz), taking C to be the whole Z space instead evaluates the X,Y marginal. The asserted Z marginal follows by taking A and B to be their whole value spaces and leaving C arbitrary.
